payload.feature:
REBASE AND FINISH STORY #288 SLICE B (execute_sequence moves to engine/sequence.rs, one function per step form, settled by StepVerdict) on branch story-288b-execute-sequence, already checked out in this worktree. HEAD is 301c247b, one commit on 78938e53.

The slice shipped (implement-story-288-split-the-en-4fea9976: residual, low), and its landing is next. But main has moved to 5eda13bf, and it now carries #403 (PR #483), which edited execute_sequence's body inside crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs:
- the attempt-outcome sites act on settled_outcome();
- a refused checkpoint rides as report.refused, beside the received outcome;
- an unresolved cleanup journals its evidence on effect/indeterminate.
The slice's commit moved that body into engine/sequence.rs, so the rebase conflicts in engine.rs and quality/suppressions.txt.

How to resolve:
- Rebase onto origin/main.
- For engine.rs, take the slice's side of the move: execute_sequence leaves engine.rs. Then port EVERY change #403 made inside the old execute_sequence body into the corresponding function in engine/sequence.rs. Read #403's changes with `git diff 78938e53 5eda13bf -- crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs`, restricted to execute_sequence's lines at 78938e53.
- Keep the slice's shape (StepVerdict, SequenceRun, Carried, one function per form), and keep #403's semantics exactly. List each ported hunk in notes: the old engine.rs location and its new sequence.rs home.
- Changes #403 made to engine.rs outside execute_sequence stay in engine.rs, as main has them.
- For quality/suppressions.txt, take main's side, then regenerate with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions. The slice removed execute_sequence's excessive_nesting and too_many_lines expects, so the counts shrink.
- Grep every conflicted file for markers before git add and git rebase --continue.
- The move must still keep behaviour and bytes. These must pass unchanged:
  - every engine sequence test;
  - #403's engine/cleanup_tests.rs;
  - engine/contention_tests.rs;
  - the witness suites.
  Journaled events, their order and their payloads do not change.
- Every function in sequence.rs stays at CC 15 or under and 100 lines or under. Split a function if the port pushes it over. engine.rs must still shrink, and sequence.rs stays under 800 production lines.

Test stubs must not leak. Tests need GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 unset.

Gates, all clean, from the worktree root:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files and clones
- git diff --check origin/main..HEAD

Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run everything in the foreground and never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending.

Commits: the rebased slice commit (keep its message, and add one paragraph naming the rebase onto 5eda13bf and the #403 hunks ported into sequence.rs), plus at most one signed-off commit "engine: <what changed> (#288)" ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Every claim in your notes points to a command you ran and what it printed.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
```

result.notes:
Rebased story-288b-execute-sequence onto origin/main. When fetched, origin/main was 47b0d89b, not 5eda13bf. It was two commits past it: #429 (a04c9c3f) and #288 slice C (47b0d89b), and neither touches engine.rs or engine/sequence.rs, per `git diff --stat 5eda13bf origin/main -- crates/brokkr-runtime quality`. The rebase conflicted in engine.rs (one block: HEAD's whole execute_sequence against the slice's removal) and in quality/suppressions.txt. engine.rs: I took the slice's side, removing the HEAD block (old lines 2228-2680 of the conflicted file). grep for markers over engine.rs, sequence.rs and suppressions.txt printed nothing before git add. #403's changes outside execute_sequence stay in engine.rs as main has them: Unproven, Indeterminate, drive_racing, conclude_single, execute_panel, member_runs Cleanup::Settled, journal_panel_members, failed_to_start and panel_outcome.

The five #403 hunks inside the old execute_sequence, with their old line numbers from the @@ headers of `git diff 78938e53 5eda13bf -- engine.rs` and their sequence.rs homes:
(1) `let mut unproven = Unproven::Proven` (after old 2197) became a field on StepRun, `unproven: Unproven` (sequence.rs:82).
(2) Single step, `unproven = Unproven::seat(&report); match report.settled_outcome()` (old 2270): single_step sets `unproven: Unproven::seat(&report)` (:311) and SpawnFailed sets Unproven::Proven (:303), as the old initial value did. tailed_outcome now takes &AttemptReport and matches report.settled_outcome() (:671).
(3) Panel step, `unproven = Unproven::panel(&reports)` (after old 2314): panel_step (:345), evaluated before panel_outcome consumes the reports.
(4) Dialect step, `dialect_attempt_outcome(..., &mut unproven)` (old 2390-2399): dialect_step (:410-414).
(5) Step indeterminate, json!(Indeterminate{..., unproven}) (old 2431-2434): step_result gains an `unproven` parameter (:471, 7 args including self, within the ceiling) and passes it to end_indeterminate (:483). end_indeterminate (:644) now journals the typed Indeterminate payload. Its three other callers pass Unproven::Proven (:365 needs-change, :549 change identifier, :575 contradiction), which the old code journaled as plain json! with no unproven. Proven is #403's untagged default and adds no field, so their bytes do not change. The witness and sequence suites below pass unchanged.

quality/suppressions.txt: I took main's side (13/35), then ran the check. It printed right-hand counts of 12 excessive_nesting and 34 too_many_lines once the resolved files were staged; before staging, git ls-files had listed the unmerged engine.rs three times and printed 16/33/40. The seat sandbox refuses env prefixes and export, so `BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test` could not run here. I wrote the two numbers the test printed by hand, and `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions` then passed: 6 passed, 1 ignored. GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: the seat could not unset them, but `git config --show-origin --get-regexp . | grep 'command line'` printed nothing, so no env-injected config was present.

The gates, on HEAD 673c40a0, all pass:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check: fmt-ok.
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings: clippy-ok.
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime: runtime-ok, 26 test-result lines all ok. The lib has 518 passed, among them 30 engine::cleanup_tests and contention_tests lines ok, and witness_digests has 6 passed.
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test witness_journal: 2 passed.
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions: ok.
- typos --hidden: ok.
- quality/ratchet.sh files: 'file size holds'.
- quality/ratchet.sh clones: 'duplication holds'.
- git diff --check origin/main..HEAD: ok.
- compile --bundle bundles/self: compiled-ok.
No test file differs from origin/main: `git diff --stat origin/main` over the engine and tests dirs lists only sequence.rs.

Sizes: engine.rs is 4099 lines on main and 3650 now; sequence.rs is 702 (under 800). By cargo-crap 0.5.0 --missing optimistic on sequence.rs, the highest CC is sequence_step at 12, then single_step, settle_step and between_steps at 6; every function is at or under 15. Clippy's too_many_lines threshold of 100 passes.

Commit 673c40a0 is GPG-signed (%G? = G) and keeps the author and the original message, with one paragraph added naming the rebase and the five ported hunks. There is no second commit, and nothing was pushed. scripts/coverage-exact.sh was not run; the controller runs it, so it is pending.

Follow-up, a gap that predates this slice and that I did not widen to close: no test drives an unresolved cleanup through a sequence step. Two mutations together survived the whole brokkr-runtime suite (all ok, lib 518 passed): step_result passing Unproven::Proven instead of `unproven`, and tailed_outcome matching report.outcome.clone() instead of settled_outcome(). #403's cleanup_tests bind dialect_attempt_outcome, Unproven::panel and the single-seat conclude_single path. They bind nothing in execute_sequence, and the test files are byte-identical to main's, so main's execute_sequence hunks are equally unbound. Binding them needs a seam that hands a sequence step an AttemptReport, or a stub driver that leaves a real stray process. I name it rather than build it, to stay in scope.

cargo test --workspace: 93 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

members.adversarial:
Adversarial read of the one commit over origin/main 47b0d89b: 673c40a0. git diff origin/main..HEAD touches only engine.rs (import reorganized, execute_sequence removed), new engine/sequence.rs, and quality/suppressions.txt. I mapped the old execute_sequence (git show 47b0d89b:crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs:2241-2675) onto sequence.rs statement by statement: per step the gate arm, then single_step/panel_step/dialect_step, then settle_step -> step_result -> between_steps (only when !is_last) -> carry_change -> finish_sequence|checkpoint_step. Every journal site, event order, payload string, the refused closure and the SeatRecord checkpoint refusal are preserved. The vocabulary-failure path passes Vec::new() to failed_payload, which start_failure_fields returns early on (engine.rs:2900-2914), so its effect/failed payload is unchanged. The dialect needs-change early return still skips finish_gate_head_check exactly as before, and every terminal journal returns StepVerdict::Ended, so no later step can run: no fail-open, no weakened refusal. The five #403 hunks are all ported: StepRun.unproven (sequence.rs:82), single_step Unproven::seat + tailed_outcome on report.settled_outcome() (:311/:671), panel_step Unproven::panel (:345), dialect_step dialect_attempt_outcome(.., &mut unproven) (:412), step_result -> end_indeterminate typed Indeterminate (:483/:644). The three Proven end_indeterminate sites serialize byte-identically to the old plain json!: cleanup_tests.rs:186-190 pins that Proven adds no key, so re-routing needs-change, change-identifier and last-step-contradiction through Indeterminate changes no bytes. #403's changes outside execute_sequence stay in engine.rs; origin/main..HEAD changes no other engine region. No conflict markers remain and no rebase is in progress.

Gates run in the foreground from the worktree root, all exit 0: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime (lib 518 passed / 0 failed, including engine::cleanup_tests 6/6 and engine::contention_tests 24/24; integration incl. witness_digests 6/6); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions (6 passed, 1 intentionally ignored); BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 reproduced quality/suppressions.txt unchanged (hash 083c24ad before and after); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test witness_journal (2 passed); cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked (exit 0); compile bundles/self and bundles/verify (exit 0); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files ('file size holds') and clones ('duplication holds'); git diff --check origin/main..HEAD (clean).

LOW finding (decision 0071 ruling 9, tests that bind): the #403 cleanup-evidence semantics this port adds to sequence.rs are not bound by any test. No test drives a sequence step to an unresolved process tree: every execute_sequence call site passes steps/inputs (no AttemptReport seam), the test drivers build reports through engine/tests.rs::report(), which sets cleanup: Cleanup::Settled (tests.rs:857), and every Cleanup::Unresolved in the suite goes to a non-sequence seam (failed_to_start directly at agent_tests.rs:220; conclude_single / dialect_attempt_outcome / Unproven::panel at cleanup_tests.rs:16,192; settled.carry at contention_tests.rs:1238). The one sequence indeterminate test, sequence_execution_covers_spawn_failure_and_indeterminate_terminal_shapes (tests.rs:2071), uses a settled report and asserts only that the reason contains 'stderr tail'. Concrete consequence: a compiling mutation that passes Unproven::Proven instead of the step's unproven inside step_result, or that matches report.outcome instead of report.settled_outcome() in tailed_outcome, survives the entire workspace suite and would silently drop the received/cleanup fields contracts/effect-cleanup.v1.schema.json requires for an unresolved sequence step. The shipped code is correct by inspection (I traced the unresolved path: settled_outcome -> Indeterminate, Unproven::seat/panel -> cleanup_evidence, end_indeterminate -> typed Indeterminate), so this is a binding gap, not a wrong output today. It is low, not medium: no new test was added that cannot fail, and the exact-coverage gate counts lines/branches, which these values do not alter. No security residual: no refusal was weakened and no fail-open path exists. Read-only: nothing was fixed, staged or committed.
